Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
17	
18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
60	- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

# Error taxonomy — 13 codes

Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.

| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |

**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.

**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.

- Unconditional refresh-at-boot (no client-side expiry math) trades one always-on network round trip for zero clock-skew bugs; revisit only if the 300ms-threshold UX proves this too slow in practice.
- Mid-session reactive refresh-on-401 is deliberately deferred to Story 1.5 (the overlay) rather than solved here with a second mechanism.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/features/auth lib/core/network lib/main.dart --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches (RNF08) -- widened to include `lib/main.dart`, where this story's own new UI (the `StreamBuilder`/boot-loading screen) actually lives

## Suggested Review Order

**Domain contract (entry point)**

- The one new DI-singleton access point for session validity — a stream plus a one-shot restore call, nothing else.
  [`session_repository.dart:11`](../../lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart#L11)
- The two-state status the epic's AD requires — no third "expired-mid-session" state, deliberately deferred to Story 1.5.
  [`session_status.dart:1`](../../lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart#L1)

**Boot-time restore (the core mechanism)**

- `restoreSession()` — unconditional refresh, no client-side expiry math; the server is the sole source of truth.
  [`session_repository_impl.dart:74`](../../lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart#L74)
- Only a backend-confirmed dead token clears storage; any other failure leaves it untouched so the next boot retries.
  [`session_repository_impl.dart:96-110`](../../lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart#L96-L110)
- Replay-last-value stream: a late subscriber still sees current status immediately, not just future changes.
  [`session_repository_impl.dart:46-66`](../../lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart#L46-L66)

**Refresh-token persistence**

- `saveSession`/`clearSession` write the refresh token first — the one field `restoreSession()` actually keys its next-boot decision on.
  [`access_token_provider.dart:60-86`](../../lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart#L60-L86)
- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` now persists the refresh token too, not just the access token.
  [`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-62`](../../lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart#L46-L62)
- `auth-refresh`'s own body/response shape can't reuse `_post`/`AuthResponseDto` — decodes the nested `session` object directly.
  [`auth_remote_data_source.dart:26-48`](../../lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart#L26-L48)

**Boot UI (main.dart)**

- `home` branches on `statusStream` instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`; `restoreSession()` fires once in `initState`.
  [`main.dart:47-63`](../../lib/main.dart#L47-L63)
- Blank for the happy path, spinner only past RNF01's 300ms threshold — a slow/offline boot no longer looks frozen.
  [`main.dart:130-170`](../../lib/main.dart#L130-L170)

**Wiring (DI)**

- `SessionRepository` registered as a singleton with `dispose:` wired into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle.
  [`auth_injection.dart:33-39`](../../lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart#L33-L39)

**Tests (peripherals)**

- The four I/O-matrix rows plus the two exception-mapping paths and the replay-semantics check.
  [`session_repository_impl_test.dart:1`](../../test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart#L1)
- `refresh()`'s write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline) per RNF09.
  [`auth_remote_data_source_test.dart:1`](../../test/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source_test.dart#L1)
- Real `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` round-trip coverage for the new session methods.
  [`access_token_provider_test.dart:1`](../../test/core/network/access_token_provider_test.dart#L1)
- `auth-refresh` proven over the real pipeline with the anon-key bearer, mirroring the existing `auth-login` case.
  [`network_pipeline_integration_test.dart:1`](../../test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart#L1)
- Both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home) driven through the real composition root.
  [`main_test.dart:1`](../../test/main_test.dart#L1)

99	+## Intent
100	+
101	+**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.
102	+
103	+**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.
104	+
105	+## Boundaries & Constraints
106	+
107	+**Always:**
108	+- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
109	+- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
110	+- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
111	+- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
112	+- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
113	+- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).
114	+
115	+**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.
116	+
117	+**Never:**
118	+- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
119	+- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
120	+- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.
121	+
122	+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
123	+
124	+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
125	+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
126	+| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
127	+| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
128	+| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
129	+| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
130	+| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |

+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.
+
+**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
+- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
+- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
+- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
+- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
+- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).
+
+**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.
+
+**Never:**
+- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
+- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
+- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
+| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
+| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
+| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
+| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |
+
+</frozen-after-approval>

+**Acceptance Criteria:**
+- Given a stored refresh token the backend accepts, when the app launches, then the user reaches the authenticated placeholder with no login prompt and no visible loading UI in the happy path (<300ms).
+- Given no stored session or a refresh token the backend rejects, when the app launches, then the user lands on `AuthScreen` with no error message shown.

+# Story 1.2 — Design Token System & Core Component Library
+
+## Context
+
+Story 1.2 delivered `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` and three shared widgets
+(`AppButton`, `AppTextField`, `Avatar`). Each component already had thorough
+*isolated* widget tests (one component at a time, checked against
+`DesignTokens` values). The gap: nothing proved the shared text-field/button
+primitives work together the way a consuming screen composes them — user
+keystrokes, taps, and focus changes flowing through multiple widgets in the
+same tree. That is a gap in the component library's own test coverage, not a
+screen's — it holds regardless of which feature consumes the widgets, and
+still no device/simulator/CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md), so a traditional
+on-device E2E run isn't possible either way.
+
+(Story 1.3's actual login screen, `auth_screen.dart`, already shipped by the
+time of this round of patches — see `git log`. Its own `auth_screen_test.dart`
+is BLoC/cubit-focused and doesn't exercise raw widget interaction such as
+obscured-text-while-typing, keyboard-action focus movement, or a disabled
+button's `onPressed` actually staying `null`; this harness is not a stand-in
+for that screen, it covers what that screen's test suite does not.)
+
+## Generated Tests
+
+### Composition/interaction tests (shared widget library, user-driven)
+
+- [x] `test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart` — a
+      `StatefulWidget` test harness (test-only, not shipped code) composing
+      two `AppTextField`s + one `AppButton` the way a form screen will.
+      Covers, through real taps and keystrokes:
+  - submit button stays disabled (`onPressed: null`) until both fields are
+    non-empty, and enables once they are.
+  - tapping the enabled button delivers the typed e-mail and senha values.
+  - an invalid e-mail surfaces the error border (`colorError`, 1.5px
+    `borderWidthEmphasis`) and error text, and never calls the submit
+    callback.
+  - correcting the e-mail after an invalid submit and resubmitting clears
+    the error and calls the submit callback.
+  - pressing the keyboard's "next" action on the e-mail field moves focus
+    to the senha field (`TextField`'s built-in default behavior — no extra
+    wiring needed).
+  - the senha field stays obscured while typing.
+  - a disabled button's `onPressed` is actually `null`, and tapping it never
+    fires the callback.
+  - the whole composed form renders with no overflow/exception at a 3.0x
+    Dynamic Type scale.
+
+No new API endpoints exist for this story (pure UI/design-system work).
+
+## Coverage
+
+- Core component library: unit-level coverage already complete
+  (pre-existing, one widget at a time); this pass adds the missing
+  cross-component interaction coverage.
+- UI features: Story 1.3's login/signup screen is covered by its own
+  `auth_screen_test.dart` (BLoC-focused); this harness covers the shared
+  widgets' interaction behavior independent of any one screen.
+

@@ -32,4 +53,35 @@ class SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider implements AccessTokenProvider {

+  }) async {

+    // (no atomic multi-key transaction in `flutter_secure_storage`), so if
+    // the second write below ever fails, this order leaves the *refresh*
+    // token as the backend's latest-issued one — the next boot's

+    // `auth-refresh` at all, so clearing it first guarantees a
+    // backend-confirmed-dead token is never retried even if the
+    // access-token delete below then fails.
+    await _storage.delete(key: _refreshKey);
+    await _storage.delete(key: _key);

  Review of the story-1-4 diff (silent session refresh & persistence). Findings below, no severity/ranking implied.
  
  - `lib/main.dart`'s `_CerneAppState.build()` passes `_sessionRepository.statusStream` directly into `StreamBuilder(stream: ...)`, but `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream` (`lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart`, the `Stream<SessionStatus>.multi(...)` getter) constructs and returns a brand-new `Stream` object on every single access. Every rebuild of `_CerneAppState` therefore hands `StreamBuilder` a different stream *instance* (even though it's backed by the same controller), which makes `StreamBuilder.didUpdateWidget` cancel and resubscribe on every rebuild instead of reusing one subscription. This never gets exercised by any test because `main_test.dart` only ever triggers a single build before `pumpAndSettle()`.
  
  - The new "auth-refresh goes out with the anon-key bearer…" test added to `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart` queues a response fixture shaped `{'session': {...}}` (no `data` wrapper). Every other place in this diff — `AuthRemoteDataSource.refresh()`'s own parsing (`json['data']['session']`), `auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`'s `_refreshBody()` helper, and the spec's own Code Map note ("`{data: {session}}`, no `user`") — uses `{data: {session: {...}}}`. This particular test calls the raw `apiClient.post(...)` rather than `dataSource.refresh(...)`, so the mismatched shape doesn't fail it, but it leaves a misleading example of the real `auth-refresh` response shape in the test suite.
  
  - `SessionRepositoryImpl.dispose()` and the `get_it` `dispose:` wiring in `auth_injection.dart` have no direct test asserting the underlying `StreamController` is actually closed. More importantly, nothing in `_emit()`/`restoreSession()` checks `_statusController.isClosed` before calling `.add(...)`; if `dispose()` (e.g. via `sl.reset()`/`resetCoreDependencies()`) ever races with an in-flight `restoreSession()` call, `.add()` after `.close()` throws an uncaught `StateError` that escapes outside the `Either<Failure, T>` contract the rest of the repository is careful to maintain (RNF09's spirit) — it's only incidentally caught at `main.dart`'s own `catchError` call site, not for any other caller.
  
  - The `_BootLoadingScreen` 300ms blank-then-spinner behavior (`lib/main.dart`), which the spec explicitly calls out as this story's own new UI and the reason RNF01's grep was widened to `lib/main.dart`, has zero test coverage. Every `main_test.dart` test drives through `pumpAndSettle()`, which fast-forwards past the internal `Timer`, so neither "stays blank below 300ms" nor "shows the spinner once past 300ms" is ever actually asserted.
  
  - `_CerneAppState._asUnauthenticated` (the `catchError` handler wrapping `restoreSession()`) is never exercised by any test. The code comment calls it "cheap insurance" since `restoreSession()` is documented to never throw, but that means this branch currently has no coverage at all and a future refactor could silently break it without any test noticing.
  
  - `AccessTokenProvider.saveSession`/`clearSession` (`lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart`) carry a carefully-reasoned comment about write ordering (refresh token written/cleared first so a mid-sequence failure is "self-healing" on the next boot), but no test verifies that ordering (e.g. via `verifyInOrder` against a mocked storage, or by simulating the second write throwing). The safety property the comment describes is currently asserted only in prose.
  
  - The diff bundles `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s and `AuthCubit.passwordChanged()`'s behavior changes (`lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart`) — switching `toggleMode` to go through `copyWith` so an in-flight `status` survives, and making `passwordChanged` also clear `emailError` — with no test that can observe either fix (every existing `toggleMode()`/`passwordChanged()` call site in the suite exercises only the default/idle state). `deferred-work.md` itself admits this gap, but the diff still ships an observable behavior change with no regression test backing it.
  
  - This diff mixes at least three stories' worth of changes under one "story 1.4" label: pure reformatting across `app_button.dart`/`app_text_field.dart`/`avatar.dart`/several test files, spec-document edits for stories 1.2 and 1.3 (new Review Findings sections, test-summary rewrites), and the actual session-refresh feature work. That makes the functional diff for 1.4 much harder to isolate and review, and would make bisecting a regression to "which story caused this" harder later.
  
  - `SessionRepositoryImpl.restoreSession()`'s "no stored refresh token" branch (fresh install / post-logout) returns `left(Failure.authExpired(message: 'No stored session to restore'))`. Reusing `AuthExpired` for "a session that never existed" is explicitly sanctioned by the spec's Boundaries section, but nothing in the code distinguishes this from an actually-expired token — if this `Left` is ever logged, surfaced in telemetry, or inspected by a future caller, "never had a session" and "had one that expired" are indistinguishable.
  
  - Nothing guards against `restoreSession()` being invoked more than once per app lifetime. The whole "boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally" design (and the refresh-token self-healing rationale in `access_token_provider.dart`) rests entirely on `_CerneAppState.initState()` running exactly once. If `CerneApp` is ever remounted (hot reload, a future parent widget tearing it down and rebuilding it, a wrapping screen), a second `restoreSession()` call could fire against a refresh token the first call already rotated away, incorrectly logging the user out — and there's no test or runtime guard for this.
  
  - The domain-layer `SessionRepository` interface (`lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`) carries a `dispose()` method whose entire purpose is `get_it`'s lifecycle wiring. That's an infrastructure/DI concern expressed in the domain contract — it doesn't literally violate RNF06 (no flutter/data imports), but it's a lifecycle-management leak into what's otherwise meant to be a pure business-rule interface, and every other domain repository in the codebase has no equivalent method.
  
  Files most relevant to these findings: `lib/main.dart`, `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart`, `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`, `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart`, `lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart`, `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart`, `test/main_test.dart`, `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md`.

None of the tests I read would fail, since none of them drive `clearSession()` to throw from inside this specific branch — `fvm flutter test` would stay green.

None of the tests I read would fail, since none exercises `passwordChanged` after `emailError` has been set.
  - **Consequence:** a regression reintroducing the asymmetric-clear bug (stale e-mail error lingering after an unrelated password edit) ships undetected.
  - **Suggested test shape:** extend the existing malformed-email cubit/screen tests with a follow-up step that calls `passwordChanged`/edits the senha field after `emailError` is set, and asserts the e-mail error is now cleared.
  
  ## Other findings
  
  - `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md`'s new entries already document a closely related, narrower gap on the same `AuthCubit` methods — `toggleMode()`'s `copyWith`-based status preservation has no test that sets `status` non-idle before calling it. I traced this one specifically and did not report it as a formal gap: `toggleMode`'s only real call site (`AuthScreen`'s ghost-toggle button, `lib/features/auth/presentation/screens/auth_screen.dart`) disables the button whenever `isSubmitting` is true, and every failure path immediately resets `status` back to `ResourceIdle` in the same `emit`, so there is no realistic way for the production UI to invoke `toggleMode()` while `status` is non-default — unlike the `passwordChanged`/`emailError` case above, which is reachable through ordinary use of the real screen.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

1	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
2	
3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	import '../entities/session_status.dart';
5	
6	/// The epic's ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (AD) —
7	/// every later consumer (Story 1.5's overlay, Story 1.6's `go_router`
8	/// redirect, Epic 4/RF07) listens to [statusStream] rather than re-deriving
9	/// session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream (RNF09 — still
10	/// `Either<Failure, T>` for the one-shot [restoreSession] call).
11	abstract class SessionRepository {
12	  /// Broadcast stream of the current session status. Emits nothing until
13	  /// [restoreSession] (or a later story's own trigger) completes at least
14	  /// once — a `StreamBuilder` with no data yet is the brief-blank boot state
15	  /// `main.dart` relies on (RNF01's 300ms threshold).
16	  Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream;
17	
18	  /// Boot-time, unconditional refresh: exchanges any stored refresh token
19	  /// for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, persists the result, and emits the
20	  /// outcome on [statusStream]. No client-side expiry math — the server is
21	  /// the sole source of truth for validity.
22	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();
23	
24	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
25	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, so `resetCoreDependencies()`
26	  /// (`sl.reset()`) closes it instead of leaking a `StreamController` on
27	  /// every test teardown.
28	  Future<void> dispose();
29	}
30

1	import 'package:flutter_bloc/flutter_bloc.dart';
2	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
3	
4	import '../../../../core/resource.dart';
5	import '../../domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart';
6	import '../../domain/validators/auth_validators.dart';
7	import 'auth_state.dart';
8	
9	/// Drives Tela 0.1a. Calls [AuthRepository] directly (no use-case — Code Map:
10	/// this story's scope is small enough that an extra indirection layer isn't
11	/// justified yet); a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as
12	/// a dependency (architecture spine), so this takes the repository port.
13	class AuthCubit extends Cubit<AuthState> {
14	  AuthCubit(this._authRepository) : super(const AuthState());
15	
16	  final AuthRepository _authRepository;
17	
18	  /// Toggles login/signup — same screen, not a navigation (epics.md Story
19	  /// 1.3 AC). Keeps whatever the user already typed; clears any error from
20	  /// the previous mode's attempt. Goes through `copyWith` (rather than a raw
21	  /// `AuthState(...)`) so an in-flight `status` is never silently reset to
22	  /// idle by this call.
23	  void toggleMode() {
24	    emit(
25	      state.copyWith(
26	        mode: state.mode == AuthMode.login ? AuthMode.signUp : AuthMode.login,
27	        clearEmailError: true,
28	        clearPasswordError: true,
29	        clearFormError: true,
30	      ),
31	    );
32	  }
33	
34	  void emailChanged(String value) {
35	    emit(
36	      state.copyWith(
37	        email: value,
38	        clearEmailError: true,
39	        clearPasswordError: true,
40	        clearFormError: true,
41	      ),
42	    );
43	  }
44	
45	  void passwordChanged(String value) {
46	    emit(
47	      state.copyWith(
48	        password: value,
49	        clearEmailError: true,
50	        clearPasswordError: true,
51	        clearFormError: true,
52	      ),
53	    );
54	  }
55	
56	  /// Validates locally first — a malformed email (or empty password) blocks
57	  /// submit *before* any round trip (epics.md Story 1.3 AC), each as its own
58	  /// single-field error so only the offending field is ever bordered. Only
59	  /// once local validation passes does it call `auth-signup`/`auth-login`
60	  /// with exactly `{email, password}` (the e-mail trimmed — stray
61	  /// leading/trailing whitespace must never reach the backend and risk a
62	  /// spurious `AUTH_INVALID`), saving the access token (via the repository)
63	  /// before this resolves.
64	  Future<void> submit() async {
65	    if (state.isSubmitting) {
66	      return;
67	    }
68	
69	    final emailError = validateEmail(state.email);
70	    if (emailError != null) {
71	      emit(
72	        state.copyWith(
73	          emailError: emailError,
74	          clearPasswordError: true,
75	          clearFormError: true,
76	        ),
77	      );
78	      return;
79	    }
80	
81	    final passwordError = validatePassword(state.password);
82	    if (passwordError != null) {
83	      emit(
84	        state.copyWith(
85	          passwordError: passwordError,
86	          clearEmailError: true,
87	          clearFormError: true,
88	        ),
89	      );
90	      return;
91	    }
92	
93	    emit(
94	      state.copyWith(
95	        status: const ResourceLoading<Unit>(),
96	        clearEmailError: true,
97	        clearPasswordError: true,
98	        clearFormError: true,
99	      ),
100	    );
101	
102	    final trimmedEmail = state.email.trim();
103	    final result = state.mode == AuthMode.login
104	        ? await _authRepository.logIn(
105	            email: trimmedEmail,
106	            password: state.password,
107	          )
108	        : await _authRepository.signUp(
109	            email: trimmedEmail,
110	            password: state.password,
111	          );
112	
113	    result.match(
114	      (failure) => emit(
115	        state.copyWith(
116	          status: const ResourceIdle<Unit>(),
117	          formError: failure.message,
118	        ),
119	      ),
120	      // Clears the typed password once it's done its job — the access
121	      // token is already persisted by now, so there's no reason for the
122	      // plaintext value to keep sitting in this (DI-singleton, long-lived)
123	      // cubit's state after success.
124	      (_) => emit(
125	        state.copyWith(status: const ResourceData<Unit>(unit), password: ''),
126	      ),
127	    );
128	  }
129	}

input.new_string:
- Given a successful signup/login, when `AuthRepositoryImpl` returns, then both the access token and refresh token are persisted, unchanged `Either<Failure,T>` signature (RNF09).

### Review Findings

- [ ] [Review][Decision] Partial `saveSession()` write failure during first login/signup can silently re-authenticate the user on the next launch, despite being told login failed — `AccessTokenProvider.saveSession()` writes the refresh token first, then the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:60-75`). If the backend call succeeds but the *second* (access-token) write throws, `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:57-64`) surfaces `Left(malformedResponse)` — the user sees "login failed" and stays on the login screen — while the new refresh token is already durably persisted. On the next app launch, `restoreSession()` finds that valid token, calls `auth-refresh`, and silently logs the user in despite the earlier failure message. Neither the spec nor `saveSession`'s own ordering rationale addresses this case. Needs a decision: roll back/clear the refresh token on access-token-write failure, treat the partial write as a (degraded) success since the backend-side account action already succeeded, or something else. [lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:60-75]
- [ ] [Review][Decision] `restoreSession()`'s `catchError` "insurance" doesn't actually unblock the UI if it's ever triggered — `_CerneAppState.initState()` wraps `restoreSession()` in `unawaited(... .catchError(_asUnauthenticated))` (`main.dart:54-75`), commented as "cheap insurance" against an unhandled zone exception. Today this is dead code, since every repository method in this diff returns `Either` and never throws. But if a future regression ever breaks that invariant, `_asUnauthenticated` only logs and returns a `Left` for a `Future` that `unawaited` already discards — it never reaches `statusStream`, so `StreamBuilder` stays on `!snapshot.hasData` (`_BootLoadingScreen`) forever, with no recovery path short of restarting the app. Actually fixing this means giving `main.dart` a way to force-emit `unauthenticated` from outside `SessionRepositoryImpl`, which widens the frozen spec's closed interface ("the ONE new DI-singleton access point... no second stream"). Needs a decision: accept the current insurance as sufficient (it only matters if another invariant is already broken), or extend the interface to make it a real fallback. [lib/main.dart:54-75]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `statusStream` getter returns a new `Stream.multi` instance on every access; `main.dart` passes it directly into `StreamBuilder` instead of caching it — currently inert because `_CerneAppState.build()` only runs once (no `setState`, no `InheritedWidget` dependency), but it's a latent resubscription/flash-to-boot-screen bug waiting for any future rebuild trigger. Fix: cache `late final Stream<SessionStatus> _statusStream = _sessionRepository.statusStream;` once in `_CerneAppState` and reference that field in `build()`. [lib/main.dart:82]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] No `isClosed` guard before `_statusController.add()` in `_emit()`; `dispose()` closes that same controller. If `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s `sl.reset()`) ever runs while a `restoreSession()` call is still in flight, the pending `.add()` throws an unhandled `StateError` — not exercised by any current test, but a real race the moment DI is torn down with a boot restore still pending (dev hot-restart, a future logout-reset flow). Fix: guard `_emit()` with `if (!_statusController.isClosed) { ... }`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:68]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_BootLoadingScreen`'s 300ms blank→spinner `Timer` logic has zero test coverage — explicitly called out by the spec as this story's own new UI (the reason RNF01's verification grep was widened to `lib/main.dart`), but every `main_test.dart` boot test uses `pumpAndSettle()`, which fast-forwards past the internal `Timer`. Neither "stays blank below 300ms" nor "shows spinner past 300ms" is ever asserted. Fix: add a widget test using `tester.pump(duration)` (not `pumpAndSettle`) to assert the blank state before 300ms and the spinner after. [lib/main.dart:137]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `readRefreshToken()` returning a non-null empty string isn't treated as "no session" — `restoreSession()` only null-checks the result (`session_repository_impl.dart:86`), so a stored empty-string refresh token (the response schema has no `minLength` on this field) would fire a network call to `auth-refresh` with an empty token (itself `minLength: 1` on the request) instead of short-circuiting like the no-token case. Low-impact (fails via the normal `VALIDATION_ERROR` path and still ends up `unauthenticated`), but a one-line fix. Fix: treat `refreshToken == null || refreshToken.isEmpty` as "no stored session." [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:86]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `deferred-work.md`'s new entries (added by this diff) claim `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s and `passwordChanged()`'s behavior changes are "pre-existing uncommitted work... not touched by story 1.4's diff" — but this diff does modify and ship `auth_cubit.dart`'s `toggleMode()`/`passwordChanged()`, so that framing is factually wrong regardless of where the change originated. Compounding this, `passwordChanged()`'s new symmetric `emailError` clear is reachable through the real `AuthScreen` (malformed-email submit sets `emailError`, then editing only the password field should clear it) and has no regression test in either `auth_cubit_test.dart` or `auth_screen_test.dart` — this one should be fixed now, not deferred, since it's in-scope and the fix is unambiguous. Fix: correct both `deferred-work.md` bullets' "not touched" claim, and add the missing `passwordChanged`-clears-`emailError` test. [lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:45]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s `copyWith`-based status-preservation fix has no regression test that can observe the regression it fixes. Checked reachability: its only call site is a button disabled whenever `isSubmitting` is true, and every failure path resets `status` to idle in the same `emit` as the one that sets `formError` — so there's no path in the current UI that can exercise a non-idle `status` at `toggleMode()` time. Legitimately deferred (unlike the `passwordChanged` item above), but the reason recorded in `deferred-work.md` should say "unreachable via current UI," not "not touched by story 1.4's diff." [lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:23] — deferred, pre-existing

**Code review complete.** 2 `decision-needed`, 5 `patch`, 1 `defer`, 6 dismissed as noise.

Findings written to the review findings section in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence.md`.

Dismissed as noise (no action needed): the diff spanning 3 stories' worth of changes under one label; `AuthExpired` reuse for "never had a session" vs. "actually expired" (explicitly spec-sanctioned); `restoreSession()`'s theoretical multiple-invocation risk (no reachable remount path exists); `SessionRepository.dispose()` living on the domain interface (style nit, not an RNF06 violation); the `network_pipeline_integration_test.dart` `auth-refresh` fixture's missing `data` wrapper (matches this file's existing, deliberately-simplified fixture convention); `statusStream`'s error-forwarding path (nothing in the codebase ever produces a stream error to trigger it).

Now I need your call on the two `decision-needed` findings — the code can't be correctly patched without knowing your intent:

**1. Partial `saveSession()` write failure can silently re-authenticate a user who was told login failed.**
`saveSession()` writes the refresh token first, then the access token. If the first login/signup succeeds against the backend but the second write throws, the user sees "login failed" — but the new refresh token is already saved, so next launch's boot-time `restoreSession()` silently logs them in anyway.
Options:
1. Roll back — on access-token-write failure, also clear/undo the refresh token so the whole operation fails consistently.
2. Treat as success — the backend already authenticated the account; let login succeed and trust next boot's refresh to pick up the stale access token.
3. Defer — rare edge case (a storage failure that hits exactly between two sequential writes); revisit only if it surfaces in practice.

**2. `restoreSession()`'s `catchError` "insurance" doesn't actually recover the UI if it's ever triggered.**
It's dead code today since no repository method in this diff ever throws. If that invariant breaks later, the handler only logs — it never reaches `statusStream`, so the user would be stuck on the boot screen forever instead of recovering to `AuthScreen` as the comment implies.
Options:
1. Accept as-is — it's genuinely unreachable under current invariants; just fix the comment so it doesn't overstate what it does.
2. Extend the interface — give `main.dart` a way to force-emit `unauthenticated`, which means renegotiating the frozen spec's "one new DI-singleton access point" boundary.
3. Defer — note the gap, no action now.

**HALT — reply with your choice for each (e.g. "1, 1" or "2 for the first, 3 for the second").**
PROCESSO: Use your technical judgment, following the input package.

Using technical judgment per the project's own documented conventions and the frozen-spec boundary rules in AGENTS.md:

**Decision 1 — dismissed, no code change.** `access_token_provider.dart`'s own comment already documents this exact trade-off as deliberate: write the refresh token first so a mid-sequence failure self-heals on the next boot, accepting the access token staying stale as "the lesser problem." The worst-case outcome is a user who saw an error message getting logged into their own account for free — not a security issue, just a narrow UX wrinkle requiring a storage failure that hits exactly the second of two sequential writes immediately after a successful backend auth call. Reworking this (e.g., rollback) would mean issuing more storage calls on a channel that's already failing, which is less reliable than the current self-healing design, not more. I'm accepting the existing design as intentional.

**Decision 2 — downgraded to patch, comment-only fix.** The `SessionRepository` interface is explicitly `<frozen-after-approval>` in the spec — widening it to add a force-emit escape hatch would mean renegotiating that frozen intent for a path that's provably unreachable today (every method in this call chain returns `Either` and never throws, per the codebase's own RNF09 convention). 9	/// Drives [AuthScreen]: mode, the two field values, their errors, and the
10	/// in-flight submit status.
11	///
12	/// [emailError] and [passwordError] are each single-field, pre-network local
13	/// validation errors — set independently, one per field, never together
14	/// (`AuthCubit.submit` checks email first and returns before ever touching
15	/// password validation). [formError] is reserved for an actual backend-call
16	/// failure (`AUTH_INVALID`/network/any other `Failure`) — it never overlaps
17	/// with either local error, since `submit` only reaches the network call
18	/// once both local checks already passed.
19	class AuthState {
20	  const AuthState({
21	    this.mode = AuthMode.login,
22	    this.email = '',
23	    this.password = '',
24	    this.emailError,
25	    this.passwordError,
26	    this.formError,
27	    this.status = const ResourceIdle<Unit>(),
28	  });
29	
30	  final AuthMode mode;
31	  final String email;
32	  final String password;
33	
34	  /// Inline "E-mail inválido" from local validation. Shown under the e-mail
35	  /// field only.
36	  final String? emailError;
37	
38	  /// Inline "Senha obrigatória" from local validation. Shown under the
39	  /// senha field only — unlike [formError], this never borders the e-mail
40	  /// field too (the e-mail value already passed its own check).
41	  final String? passwordError;
42	
43	  /// `AUTH_INVALID`/`Failure.message` from the backend call. Shown once,
44	  /// under the senha field, while *both* fields get the error border (the
45	  /// e-mail field via `errorText: ''`, border-only).
46	  final String? formError;
47	
48	  final Resource<Unit> status;
49	
50	  bool get isSubmitting => status is ResourceLoading<Unit>;
51	
52	  AuthState copyWith({
53	    AuthMode? mode,
54	    String? email,
55	    String? password,
56	    String? emailError,
57	    bool clearEmailError = false,
58	    String? passwordError,
59	    bool clearPasswordError = false,
60	    String? formError,
61	    bool clearFormError = false,
62	    Resource<Unit>? status,
63	  }) {
64	    return AuthState(
65	      mode: mode ?? this.mode,
66	      email: email ?? this.email,
67	      password: password ?? this.password,
68	      emailError: clearEmailError ? null : (emailError ?? this.emailError),
69	      passwordError:
70	          clearPasswordError ? null : (passwordError ?? this.passwordError),
71	      formError: clearFormError ? null : (formError ?? this.formError),
72	      status: status ?? this.status,
73	    );
74	  }
75	
76	  @override
77	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
78	      identical(this, other) ||
79	      (other is AuthState &&
80	          other.mode == mode &&
81	          other.email == email &&
82	          other.password == password &&
83	          other.emailError == emailError &&
84	          other.passwordError == passwordError &&
85	          other.formError == formError &&

91	        email,
92	        password,

97	      );

102	      'emailError: $emailError, passwordError: $passwordError, '
103	      'formError: $formError, status: $status)';
104	}

83	### Review Findings
84	
85	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_asUnauthenticated`'s comment overstates what `restoreSession()`'s `catchError` "insurance" (`main.dart:54-75`) actually does — it suppresses an unhandled zone exception, but since the whole call is `unawaited`, its return value is discarded and never reaches `statusStream`; it does NOT unblock the UI from `_BootLoadingScreen`. Today this is unreachable dead code (every repository method in this diff returns `Either` and never throws), and fixing the underlying gap for real would mean widening the frozen `SessionRepository` interface ("the ONE new DI-singleton access point... no second stream") for a path with no current trigger — not worth renegotiating the frozen spec for. Fix: reword the comment to say it only prevents an unhandled zone exception, not that it recovers the UI. [lib/main.dart:69-75]
86	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `statusStream` getter returns a new `Stream.multi` instance on every access; `main.dart` passes it directly into `StreamBuilder` instead of caching it — currently inert because `_CerneAppState.build()` only runs once (no `setState`, no `InheritedWidget` dependency), but it's a latent resubscription/flash-to-boot-screen bug waiting for any future rebuild trigger. Fix: cache `late final Stream<SessionStatus> _statusStream = _sessionRepository.statusStream;` once in `_CerneAppState` and reference that field in `build()`. [lib/main.dart:82]
87	- [ ] [Review][Patch] No `isClosed` guard before `_statusController.add()` in `_emit()`; `dispose()` closes that same controller. If `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s `sl.reset()`) ever runs while a `restoreSession()` call is still in flight, the pending `.add()` throws an unhandled `StateError` — not exercised by any current test, but a real race the moment DI is torn down with a boot restore still pending (dev hot-restart, a future logout-reset flow). Fix: guard `_emit()` with `if (!_statusController.isClosed) { ... }`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:68]
88	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_BootLoadingScreen`'s 300ms blank→spinner `Timer` logic has zero test coverage — explicitly called out by the spec as this story's own new UI (the reason RNF01's verification grep was widened to `lib/main.dart`), but every `main_test.dart` boot test uses `pumpAndSettle()`, which fast-forwards past the internal `Timer`. Neither "stays blank below 300ms" nor "shows spinner past 300ms" is ever asserted. Fix: add a widget test using `tester.pump(duration)` (not `pumpAndSettle`) to assert the blank state before 300ms and the spinner after. [lib/main.dart:137]
89	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `readRefreshToken()` returning a non-null empty string isn't treated as "no session" — `restoreSession()` only null-checks the result (`session_repository_impl.dart:86`), so a stored empty-string refresh token (the response schema has no `minLength` on this field) would fire a network call to `auth-refresh` with an empty token (itself `minLength: 1` on the request) instead of short-circuiting like the no-token case. Low-impact (fails via the normal `VALIDATION_ERROR` path and still ends up `unauthenticated`), but a one-line fix. Fix: treat `refreshToken == null || refreshToken.isEmpty` as "no stored session." [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:86]
90	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `deferred-work.md`'s new entries (added by this diff) claim `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s and `passwordChanged()`'s behavior changes are "pre-existing uncommitted work... not touched by story 1.4's diff" — but this diff does modify and ship `auth_cubit.dart`'s `toggleMode()`/`passwordChanged()`, so that framing is factually wrong regardless of where the change originated. Compounding this, `passwordChanged()`'s new symmetric `emailError` clear is reachable through the real `AuthScreen` (malformed-email submit sets `emailError`, then editing only the password field should clear it) and has no regression test in either `auth_cubit_test.dart` or `auth_screen_test.dart` — this one should be fixed now, not deferred, since it's in-scope and the fix is unambiguous. Fix: correct both `deferred-work.md` bullets' "not touched" claim, and add the missing `passwordChanged`-clears-`emailError` test. [lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:45]
91	- [x] [Review][Defer] `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s `copyWith`-based status-preservation fix has no regression test that can observe the regression it fixes. Checked reachability: its only call site is a button disabled whenever `isSubmitting` is true, and every failure path resets `status` to idle in the same `emit` as the one that sets `formError` — so there's no path in the current UI that can exercise a non-idle `status` at `toggleMode()` time. Legitimately deferred (unlike the `passwordChanged` item above), but the reason recorded in `deferred-work.md` should say "unreachable via current UI," not "not touched by story 1.4's diff." [lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart:23] — deferred, pre-existing

Today this is unreachable dead code (every repository method in this diff returns `Either` and never throws), and fixing the underlying gap for real would mean widening the frozen `SessionRepository` interface ("the ONE new DI-singleton access point... no second stream") for a path with no current trigger — not worth renegotiating the frozen spec for. Fix: reword the comment to say it only prevents an unhandled zone exception, not that it recovers the UI. [lib/main.dart:69-75]

- [x] [Review][Patch] `statusStream` getter returns a new `Stream.multi` instance on every access; `main.dart` passes it directly into `StreamBuilder` instead of caching it — currently inert because `_CerneAppState.build()` only runs once (no `setState`, no `InheritedWidget` dependency), but it's a latent resubscription/flash-to-boot-screen bug waiting for any future rebuild trigger. Fix: cache `late final Stream<SessionStatus> _statusStream = _sessionRepository.statusStream;` once in `_CerneAppState` and reference that field in `build()`. [lib/main.dart:82]

-- [ ] [Review][Patch] No `isClosed` guard before `_statusController.add()` in `_emit()`; `dispose()` closes that same controller. If `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s `sl.reset()`) ever runs while a `restoreSession()` call is still in flight, the pending `.add()` throws an unhandled `StateError` — not exercised by any current test, but a real race the moment DI is torn down with a boot restore still pending (dev hot-restart, a future logout-reset flow). Fix: guard `_emit()` with `if (!_statusController.isClosed) { ... }`. [lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart:68]
